Here's a consolidated, day-by-day style summary of the full 12-week plan, integrating resistance training, cardio, hot yoga, cooling strategies, perimenopause considerations, bone-health nutrition, and the updated elements you requested (Phase 2 push intensity, hot yoga, cardio, and testing guidance). Start date: 2026-06-01. The schedule assumes 4 resistance days per week (A–D) plus 1 optional conditioning day (D1) and the two hot yoga sessions (Y1, Y2) and cardio days (E, F) as noted. You can rearrange days to fit the client's calendar.

Phase 1: Foundation and acclimation (Weeks 1–4)

Phase goals
- Establish technique, reintroduce controlled volume, set baselines for strength, conditioning, and symptom management.
- Implement cooling protocols, optimize sleep, set nutrition baselines focused on bone health and lean-mass preservation.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07)
- Session A: Upper Strength (Push emphasis)
  - Warm-up: 5–7 min light cardio + shoulder mobility
  - Barbell bench press: 4×5 @ 70–75% 1RM
  - Bent-over barbell row: 3×8
  - Accessory: DB shoulder press 3×10; Triceps pushdown 3×12
  - Core: Pallof press 3×12 each side
  - Cool-down: 5–8 min light cardio; cold towel 1–2 min if tolerable
- Session B: Lower Strength (Quad emphasis)
  - Warm-up: 5–7 min cardio + hip hinge drills
  - Back squat: 4×5 @ 70–75% 1RM
  - Romanian deadlift: 3×8
  - Accessory: Bulgarian split squat 3×8 per leg; Leg extension 3×12
  - Core: Hanging leg raises 3×12
  - Cool-down: Mobility + 5 min cold exposure if available
- Session C: Upper/Posterior Chain (Pull emphasis)
  - Warm-up: Band pulls, face pulls
  - Overhead press (or push press): 4×6 @ 65–70% 1RM
  - Weighted pull-ups or lat pulldown: 4×6–8
  - Accessory: Barbell/dumbbell incline row 3×10; Biceps curls 3×12
  - Core: Ab wheel rollouts 3×12
- Session D: Conditioning + Mobility (optional)
  - 20–25 min moderate cardio in cool environment
  - 15 min mobility and breathwork
  - Cooling: fans, cold towels, electrolytes
- Optional Session Y1/Y2: Hot Yoga (see Phase 1 integration)
  - Y1: 60–70 min focused on mobility (hips, spine), breathing
  - Y2: Optional recovery-focused session if energy allows

Nutrition and recovery
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day; distribute 4–5 meals with post-workout protein
- Caloric intake: maintenance ±200 kcal; adjust weekly
- Calcium 1000–1200 mg/day; Vitamin D 2000–4000 IU/day (as advised by clinician)
- Hydration: light straw urine; electrolytes on hot days
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours; wind-down routines to support symptom control

Week 2
- Slight load increases (2–5%) on main lifts if technique solid
- Maintain 4 resistance days; 1 optional cardio day
- Breathing work during cooldown; nasal breathing to reduce thermal load
- Calcium/vitamin D maintenance; consider clinician guidance on supplements

Week 3
- Session A: Upper Push/Pulling
  - Bench 4×4 @ 75–78%
  - Barbell row 4×6
  - Accessory: DB lateral raises 3×12; skull crushers 3×12
- Session B: Lower 4×5 Squat pattern
  - Back squat 4×5 @ 75%
  - Good mornings 3×8
  - Accessory: Leg curls 3×12; Calves 3×15
- Session C: Upper Pull/Posterior Chain
  - Overhead press 4×6 @ 70%
  - T-bar row or chest-supported row 4×8
  - Accessory: Face pulls 3×15; Hammer curls 3×12
- Session D: Conditioning + Mobility
  - 20–25 min cardio; mobility and breathing work
- Optional: Y2 or light cardio day if energy allows

Week 4 (Deload Week)
- Volume down ~40–50%; main lifts ~60–65% 1RM
- Emphasize technique, recovery, sleep, hydration
- Maintain cooling strategies and hydration

Phase 2: Strength progression and heat-management (Weeks 5–8)

Phase goals
- Increase upper-push intensity, maintain lower-body strength, integrate heat-management and bone health priorities with autoregulation.

Week 5
- Session A: Upper Push/Row (Push intensity up)
  - Bench press: 4×5 @ 82–85% 1RM
  - Barbell row: 4×6 @ 70–75%
  - Accessory: Incline DB press 3×8–10; Triceps pushdown 3×12
  - Core: Pallof press 3×12 per side
  - Cool-down: Cool environment cardio + cooling
- Session B: Lower Strength + Posterior Chain
  - Squat: 4×5 @ 78–82%
  - Romanian deadlift: 3×8
  - Accessory: Reverse lunges 3×8 per leg; Leg curl 3×12
- Session C: Upper Press + Pull (Push emphasis)
  - Push press: 4×5 @ 72–78%
  - Lat pulldown: 4×8
  - Accessory: Lateral raises 3×12; Cable face pulls 3×15
- Session D: Conditioning / Heat Management
  - 20–25 min moderate cardio in cool environment
  - Post-workout cooldown with breathwork

Week 6
- Session A: Upper Push Density
  - Bench press: 4×4 @ 85–87%
  - Barbell row: 4×6 @ 72–76%
  - Accessory: DB floor press 3×8; Triceps extensions 3×12
- Session B: Lower Strength
  - Squat: 4×5 @ 80–82%
  - Good mornings: 3×8
  - Accessory: Leg curls 3×12; Calves 3×15
- Session C: Upper Push + Pull
  - Overhead press: 4×5 @ 70–75%
  - Weighted chin-ups or lat pulldown: 4×8
  - Accessory: Dumbbell row 3×10; Face pulls 3×15
- Session D: Conditioning / Heat Management
  - 15–20 min intervals in controlled cooler environment; optional 2–4 min cold exposure

Week 7
- Session A: Upper Power Push
  - Bench press: 5×3 @ 86–90% (barspeed emphasis)
  - Barbell row: 4×6
  - Accessory: DB carries 2×30s; Skull crushers 3×12
- Session B: Lower Dynamic / Posterior

  - Hip hinge variations: 3×8
  - Accessory: Glute bridge 3×12; Calf raises 3×15
- Session C: Upper Pull/Push
  - Push press: 4×5 @ 75–78%
  - Weighted chin-ups or lat pulldown: 4×8
  - Accessory: Face pulls 3×15; Dumbbell curls 3×12
- Session D: Conditioning with Cooling Protocols
  - 20–25 min moderate cardio in cooler room; mobility/breathing work

Week 8 (Deload Week)
- Volume down ~40–50%; intensity 60–70% 1RM
- Prioritize technique, recovery, and cooling
- Maintain cardio at easy-to-moderate levels; ensure hydration

Phase 3: Peak strength and endurance balance, perimenopause symptom optimization (Weeks 9–12)

Phase goals
- Peak strength maintenance with higher bar speed.
- Balance higher-intensity work with lower-volume density and robust cooling.
- Introduce 1RM testing option at Week 12 if symptom-load allows.

Week 9
- Session A: Upper Strength Focus
  - Bench press: 4×4 @ 82–86%
  - Barbell row: 4×6
  - Accessory: DB side raises 3×12; Triceps rope pushdown 3×12
- Session B: Lower Strength and Power
  - Squat: 4×4 @ 83–85%
  - Hip thrust: 3×8
  - Accessory: Leg press calf 3×12; Ab wheel 3×10
- Session C: Upper Push/Pull Superset Day
  - Push press: 4×5 @ 75%
  - Pull-ups or lat pulldown: 4×8
  - Superset: DB row 3×10 with overhead carry 2×30s
- Session D: Conditioning with Heat Management
  - 15–20 min interval cardio in cool room; 3–4 rounds of 2-min easy/1-min hard
  - 10–15 min cooldown with breathwork

Week 10
- Progressive tweaks: small load increases if form is pristine
- Maintain 4 resistance days + 1 conditioning day
- Add 1–2 days of flexible recovery around symptom flares (extra rest if needed)

Week 11
- Session A: Upper Power + Endurance
  - Bench press: 4×3 @ 88–92%
  - Barbell row: 4×6
  - Accessory: Lateral raises 3×12; Triceps extensions 3×12
- Session B: Lower Power
  - Squat: 4×3 @ 88–90%
  - Romanian deadlift: 3×8
  - Accessory: Glute bridges 3×12; Tibialis raises 3×15
- Session C: Full Body Maintenance
  - Push press or dumbbell push press: 3×6
  - Pull-downs: 3×8
  - Core: 3×15 cable anti-rotation
- Session D: Cooling and Recovery
  - 20 min low-intensity cardio in cool environment
  - Post-workout cooling protocol

Week 12 (Final week, testing or taper)
- Option A: Testing week
  - 1RM test for bench press and squat (and optionally deadlift) if technique is solid and symptoms allow
  - Follow with shorter sets and longer cooldown; ensure hydration and cooling
- Option B: Taper
  - 20–30% volume reduction; main lifts at 70–75% 1RM; maintain 8–12 reps on accessory work
  - Maintain conditioning sparingly (20–25 min easy cardio or mobility-focused cardio)
- End-of-week plan
  - Post-testing cooldowns with breathwork; plan next cycle based on results and symptom profile
  - Update training loads for Phase 4 based on progress and tolerance

Hot yoga integration (two per week)
- Y1 and Y2 slots placed on lighter-demand days or recovery days
- 60–75 min sessions, focusing on hip/hamstring/spine mobility with breathwork
- Hydration and electrolyte emphasis, avoid back-to-back heavy days around yoga

Cardio (maintains aerobic fitness; non-fasted)
- 2–3 cardio sessions per week, 20–40 minutes each; mixed modalities (cycling, rowing, walking, elliptical)
- Intensity: Zone 1–3 with occasional Zone 3 work and controlled intervals, in cool environments
- Schedule around resistance training to protect recovery and bone health

Fasted HIIT replacement
- Replaced with non-fasted, cool-environment conditioning as described earlier (bike/rower intervals, tempo cardio, post-workout conditioning)

Cardio, Yoga, and Heat Management notes
- Pre-cooling and intra-workout cooling applied to all cardio and hot yoga sessions
- Hydration: consistent intake; electrolyte supplementation on hot days or long sessions
- Symptom monitoring: track vasomotor symptoms, sleep, energy, mood; adjust intensity/volume when symptoms spike

1RM testing considerations (end of Phase 3)
- If testing: plan Week 12 early in the day, cool environment
- Exercises: bench press and back squat; optionally deadlift if technique allows
- Warm-up: ramp from 40–50% 1RM to 90–95% with 2–3 warm sets
- 2–3 attempts per lift; rest 3–5 minutes; monitor RPE (aim for final attempt around RPE 9–10)
- If symptoms/fatigue high, substitute with 5RM/3RM estimates or postpone testing to Week 13–14

Data capture and progress tracking
- Record 1RM results, reps completed, bar speed (if available), RPE, symptoms, sleep, energy, hydration
- Use results to adjust Phase 4 loads and progression strategy
- Maintain a symptoms log to guide autoregulation decisions and cooling protocols

Equipment and logistics considerations
- If training in a hot environment, emphasize heat management, cooling, and hydration
- Ensure weights and bars are accessible; provide cueing for bench depth, thoracic extension, hip hinge mechanics
- Swap or modify exercises if equipment is limited (e.g., use goblet squats if no barbell)
